summary: The same Phase I grant and the same ceiling as SBIR, but structured around a formal partnership with a non-profit research institution that performs a required share of the work. Same mandatory Project Pitch gate and same three annual deadlines.
notes: WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ROUTE: the money and deadlines are identical to SBIR Phase I — same $305,000, same 6-18 months, same Project Pitch gate, same three annual deadlines — but the work-split rules are different and they bind hard. From sbir.gov/faq/eligibility-requirements: "an STTR awardee must subcontract a portion of the award to a research institution" and "SBCs must perform at least 40% and research institutions must perform at least 30% of the work." NSF 26-510 states "the proposing small business concern must also include a partner research institution in the project" and that for STTR "the PI must be an employee of the proposing small business for at least 51% of his/her time" while "the co-PI must be part of the STTR partner research institution." PRACTICAL READ: choose STTR over SBIR when the core IP or key personnel sit inside a university or non-profit lab and you want that relationship formalised and funded; choose SBIR when the work is being done in-house, because SBIR does not force 30% of the budget out the door. The 40/30 split leaves up to 30% unallocated by rule. NOT CONFIRMED: I did not find the 40%/30% figures stated on an NSF page — they come from the sbir.gov (SBA) eligibility FAQ, which is the governing authority, but verify against the current SBIR/STTR Policy Directive before budgeting. Time from submission to decision is not stated anywhere I fetched, so timeline_days is null. All Project Pitch mechanics, window caveats and the TABA/I-Corps-inclusive nature of the $305,000 described in the SBIR Phase I record apply identically here.
